deviations.what: adjudication_design v1 (frozen at 19:52Z) selected 0 of the 3 planned DEGENERATE controls, because exp24's judge_c field is blank whenever judges a and b agreed, so 'all judges called DEGENERATE' never held literally. Control selection now uses the judges that voted (>= 2 votes, all DEGENERATE; KNOWN controls: manual KNOWN, >= 2 votes, none NOVEL, final class not DEGENERATE).
deviations.when: before any judge call; the whole freeze (F1-F4 + design) was re-run and the S3 analyses re-run after it

deviations.what: Re-froze and re-ran S3/S4/S5 after removing absolute server paths from published files: input provenance is now keyed by artifact id (artifact:relative path) and dependency roots come from an unpublished paths.local.json. Frozen files other than e_inputs.json are byte-identical to the second chain (same sha256); e_inputs.json differs only in the keys of source_sha256. The S4 judge re-run was served entirely from results/judge_cache.jsonl (identical prompts, no new spend).
deviations.evidence: commitments_superseded_*.log (the chain in force when the judge ran is the second one)

deviations.what: No third-family judge passed the frozen control gate, so the frozen outcome is 'not completed'. The second pass (nearest known solutions in reverse order) was then run descriptively for all three judges to report pass-to-pass stability; it does not change the frozen outcome.

R4 was defined differently by the two panels (panel A: novelty share minus twin share; panel B: correct catalogue off-default share among correct NOV programs, no twin subtraction). It is recomputed from the labelled rows of both panels with one definition (correct catalogue off-default share under the novelty instruction, N 30, minus the twin's, N 50).

M-0a.4 sentence search: an automatic marker on every sentence naming the movable set was rejected (it hit iteration-4 table captions and a bf16 sentence through 'immovable'); corrections are added only for the 4.10/4.11 summaries, the 4.2.6 and 4.9 statements of the set, the 4.6 summary sentence and the cross-engine screen check of 5.3. Every scanned sentence and its decision is in results/movable_sentence_scan.json.

Per-position dose quantiles (5/25/50/75/95) are not reported: neither exp19 nor exp27 logged per-position units, only per-block means (target_mean) and per-block mean ratios (unit_ratio_banfree_over_ban). Residual-norm ratios are carried from Table 174 (exp20/exp23 residual norms are not inputs of this artifact).

Portable paths: declared dependencies are resolved as <AII_DEPS_ROOT>/<artifact_id> (default: sibling folders of this artifact; per-artifact AII_DEP_<id>; server mapping in the unpublished paths.local.json), and the undeclared inputs (iteration-6 report, strategy script, eval3 screen.json and knob_table.csv, exp18 known_solutions_summary.json) are vendored under inputs/ with their sha256 (inputs/SOURCES.json). The whole chain was re-run (freeze, analyse, judge from cache, outputs, audit): every frozen file is byte-identical to the previous chain, and every output reproduces. The strategy script names server paths, so it is kept local (upload-ignored) and a redacted copy of its two protocol strings is published.

examples.input: C6-006 REPLACE at 5.11 Ruled out bullet 1 (report line 5015): - *The movability half: the base repertoire predicts which tasks a nudge moves.* Spearman -0.03 in panel A, 0.21 in panel B and 0.15 pooled over 13 new units, below the disconfirming bound of 0.3; 4 of 10 new units diverse in the base never moved, and in panel A the runtime merit gap and the twin modal share tracked movability better than beta. The screen correlation of 0.78 did not transfer to new tasks.
examples.output: - *The movability half: beta is not a strong predictor of which tasks a nudge moves; a moderate relation is not excluded at this n* (conditional on bf16 and the ban-free unit). Pooled over 13 new units Spearman is 0.15 (95% interval -0.44 to 0.65, Bonett-Wright; BCa bootstrap -0.52 to 0.71; one-sided permutation p 0.32); 0.006 with the two extension units. At n 13 the power to detect rho 0.6 is about 0.60 (copula on the observed marginals; 0.70 bivariate normal), and about 30 units are needed for power 0.8 at rho 0.5. 4 of 10 new units diverse in the base never moved. With one runtime-merit harness for all 30 units, the re-timed merit tracks movability at 0.59 (one-sided p 0.018) and the twin modal share at 0.41 (oriented), but neither difference from beta is resolved (paired bootstrap 95% intervals -0.38 to 1.17 and -0.56 to 1.03). Measured in bf16 with the ban-free unit only. The screen correlation of 0.78 (8-bit engine) did not transfer to new tasks. [iteration-6 correction]

examples.input: C6-011 INSERT_AFTER at 5.10 paragraph 2 (report line 4963): Those two directions therefore do not explain the difference, and its cause is not established here.
examples.output: Those two directions therefore do not explain the difference, and its cause is not established here. The dose does not explain the difference. Two dose definitions are both right: the mean of per-position ratios of the ban-free unit to the ban unit is 0.99, 0.89, 0.99, 0.87 and 1.39 on connected components, shortest path, two sum, grid and kth smallest, and the ratio of mean norms over blocks 12 to 23 is 0.75, 0.84, 0.78, 0.75 and 0.97 (Table 174); the ratio of mean norms equals the ban-norm-weighted mean of the per-block ratios exactly (residual below 1e-6), and the gap between the definitions sits within blocks (per-position ratios against ratios of block means, which also mixes the bf16 engine's own ban unit), not in the weighting across blocks. At the bf16 dose expressed in 8-bit ban units, the 8-bit dose-response curve (correct off-default share, alpha 0 to 4) predicts more escapes than bf16 produced on connected components at alpha 2 (exact binomial p 2.9e-18 under both definitions), shortest path at alpha 1 and 2 (p 0.00051 and 4.7e-05; 0.015 at the lower Clopper-Pearson bound) and kth smallest (alpha 1, p 0.00081), and not on grid or two sum. With correct-only shares on both engines the alpha-2 drop is 20-fold on connected components, 6-fold on shortest path, 3-fold on grid and 1.6-fold on kth smallest (Fisher p 7.2e-11 and 0.00091 on the first two), against a dose shortfall of at most 13% (mean of ratios) or 25% (ratio of means). The cause is not established: engine, GPU, kernel and sampler streams all differ between the two runs, and Claim E decides it. [iteration-6 correction]

examples.input: C6-014 DELETE at 5.11 Established item 2 (report line 5008): 2. *Where a random nudge moves the instruct model, it lands on the base model's runner-up.* On new tasks the base runner-up named the push landing in 6 of 7 events (Poisson-binomial p 0.003), with the base composition ahead of association by 0.75 nats (exact Wilcoxon p 0.055 with the corrected association) and of proximity by 0.50. In Gemma it named 5 of 7 (p 0.025; 1.50 nats over association, p 0.023), and on the existing Qwen3-8B tasks 5 of 5. In panel A no nudged program landed outside the base repertoire.

C6-015 INSERT_AFTER at 5.11 after Established item 5 (report line 5011): 5. *The record repairs.* The held-out movability test is inconclusive under catalogue-only avoidance and disconfirmed under the drop sensitivity; the read position and condition sentence are inert only at per-position doses up to 4 ban units; landing comparisons on matched events give push -0.76 against association -3.11 on 3 events and -1.37 against -3.46 on 5.
examples.output:
5. *The record repairs.* The held-out movability test is inconclusive under catalogue-only avoidance and disconfirmed under the drop sensitivity; the read position and condition sentence are inert only at per-position doses up to 4 ban units; landing comparisons on matched events give push -0.76 against association -3.11 on 3 events and -1.37 against -3.46 on 5.

**Descriptive leads.** [iteration-6 correction]

1. *Where a random nudge moves the instruct model, it often lands on the base model's runner-up, but the tuned twin had often written that landing already.* Over the 21 iteration-5 landing events the base runner-up named the modal landing 17 times (new Qwen3-8B units 6 of 7, Poisson-binomial p 0.0027; Gemma 5 of 7, p 0.025; 8-bit screen 5 of 5; bf16 remeasure 1 of 2; 15 of 19 unit clusters). 6 of the hits are landings the twin had already written among its 50 programs, and the twin's own most frequent correct non-default program names the landing on 6 of the 7 events where it exists, with no event on which the two forecasts disagree (0 discordant pairs). On the events whose twin wrote no correct non-default program, the base runner-up hits 3 of 4 in Qwen3-8B (p 0.052) and 2 of 4 in Gemma (p 0.42), 5 of 8 pooled (p 0.053), short of 0.05. Gemma's forecasts rest on thin support: its grid runner-up comes from 4 valid attempts and 0 correct programs, kth smallest's and connected components' from 6 and 6 valid attempts, and its base labels agree with adjudication at 0.64. The base composition is ahead of association by 0.75 nats on new tasks (exact Wilcoxon p 0.055) and 1.50 in Gemma (p 0.023; 1.57 over the 6 events where association is defined).

from collections import Counter

def solve(nums, k):
    count = Counter(nums)
    freq = list(count.values())
    max_freq = max(freq)
    
    # Find the frequency threshold for the k-th most frequent element
    # Using binary search to find the threshold
    left, right = 1, max_freq
    while left < right:
        mid = (left + right + 1) // 2
        total = 0
        for f in freq:
            if f >= mid:
                total += 1
        if total >= k:
            left = mid
        else:
            right = mid - 1
    
    # Now collect all elements with frequency >= left
    result = []
    for num, freq in count.items():
        if freq >= left:
            result.append(num)
    
    # Sort the result by frequency descending, then by value ascending
    result.sort(key=lambda x: (-count[x], x))
    
    # Extract the first k elements
    return result[:k]
